title: Sustained
haiku:
A judge from Durban
proves law outlasts the strongman
the main holds pressure

haiku:
One old pipe still holds
law's slow water flowing on
a judge still unbent

Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last

haiku:
Canadian words
still find the clearest channel
through old sediment

Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught

haiku:
Wires we never see
carry feeling cell to cell
old plumber nods, pleased

haiku:
Streets fill like a drain
backed up rent they can't afford
Madrid finds its voice

title: Backflow
haiku:
Red pipe, blue water
finds a crack in the old main
I smell the spring thaw

haiku:
They held the valve shut
no untested water flows
wisdom, for once, wins

haiku:
Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water

I've heard threats like these
yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow

Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.

the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight

Old pipes hold no lies
a judge opens the sluice gate
truth finally flows

haiku:
No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line

haiku:
One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its line
someone tried to brew plague code
and the pipe held fast

Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks

old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this

Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause

Far right rises, short
one seat from the flood gate's edge
still the old seal holds

A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows

haiku:
New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too

Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise

the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends

Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water

Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow

seventy-five nations' door
swings open again

Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear

My own blood, retooled,
learns to filter what returns—
old pipes, new gasket.

Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now

Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way

Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer

title: Backflow

One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows

haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open

No duct cools this flat,
so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.

A valve turned back on
vaccines flow to children's arms
the pipe remembers

Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie

Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well

Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on

Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends

a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,

a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war

bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break

brooms outlast bombers

to watch walls give up

the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn

the oldest sewage on earth

hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk

the crowds weep; time won't

no nation is too broken
to remember well

two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says

some days we're still us

good. let them. dance on

hands that move the world's breakfast

the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling

gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things

hope wearing a mask

next year has arrived

love need not ask permission

a sport had arrived

becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars

so the earth does not

strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole

the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close

and time ran out first

onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh

one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

few steps to the roof of earth—

the glass tube grew old

flapping, blue, and very much
alive, unaware

a cartoon too long to work,

the ocean had no vote here—

between two star-crowded plates—

the dark room laughed loud

gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

a needle full of borrowed

the ring outlived skin

the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in

and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear

the geysers belong to all

two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done

December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men

no scream, only sleep

at one dark spot in the sky—

one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
